text: At the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
notes: The word ‘created’ (ברא - bara) in this context denotes bringing something into existence from nothing. ‘At the beginning’ is a literal translation of ‘בְּ/רֵאשִׁ֖ית’ to maintain precision. The use of ‘heavens’ and ‘earth’ reflects the literal translation of the Hebrew terms.

text: The earth was formless and void, and darkness was over the face of the deep. The Spirit of God moved over the waters.
notes: The phrase ‘formless and void’ is a standard rendering. ‘Void’ is translated as ‘void’ to maintain clarity for a technical audience. ‘Roh’ (רוּחַ) is consistently translated as ‘Spirit’. ‘Pneuma’ is a theological term, and ‘Spirit’ is a more accessible equivalent.

text: God saw the light and determined it was good. God separated the light from the darkness.
LORD called the light Day, and the darkness He called Night. Evening and morning were the first day.
LORD said, ‘Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it separate the waters from the waters.’
God created the firmament, and He separated the waters that were beneath the firmament from the waters that were above the firmament. It was as it is.
LORD called the firmament Heaven. And the evening and the morning were the second day.
The LORD said, ‘Let the waters below the sky gather into one area, and let the dry land appear.’
God called the dry land Earth, and the gathering together of the waters He called Seas. God saw that it was good.
LORD said, ‘Let the earth produce seed bearing plants and fruit trees, each producing its own kind.’
The earth produced seed bearing vegetation according to its type, and the tree produced fruit with seed within itself, according to its type. The LORD observed that it was good.
Evening and morning were the third day.
LORD said, ‘Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night, and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years.’
Let them be lights in the firmament of the heavens to give light upon the earth. It was so.
The LORD made two great lights: the greater light to govern the day, and the lesser light to govern the night. He also made the stars.
LORD established them in the firmament of heaven to illuminate the earth.
To govern the day and the night, and to separate light from darkness, God saw that it was good.
Evening and morning were the fourth day.
LORD said, ‘Let the waters produce living creatures and fowl to fly over the earth in the firmament of heaven.’
God created the great sea creatures and every living being that moves in the waters, and every type of winged fowl. God saw that it was good.
LORD blessed them and said, ‘Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the waters of the seas, and let the birds multiply on the earth.’
Evening and morning were the fifth day.
LORD said, ‘Let the earth bring forth living creatures after their kind: cattle and beasts of all kinds; and fruit-bearing trees of every kind.’
LORD made the beasts of the earth according to their kind, and the cattle according to their kind, and every creature that goes upon the earth according to its kind. LORD saw that it was good.

LORD said, ‘Let us make man in our image, after our likeness; and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, over the birds of the air, over the livestock, and over all the earth and over every living thing that moves on the earth.’
LORD created humankind in His image, in the image of God He created them; male and female created He them.
notes: The translation prioritizes clarity and a modern style while adhering to the specified terminology.

text: LORD blessed them, and LORD said to them, ‘Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth, and subdue it. Have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the air, and over every living thing that moves on the earth.’
LORD has given you every herb bearing seed, which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree, in which is the fruit of a tree yielding seed; it shall be for your nourishment.
To every living creature on earth and to every fowl in the sky and to every beast of the ground where there is life, I have given every green plant for food. It was so.
The LORD observed all that he had made, and it was good. Evening and morning were the sixth day.
God said, 'Let there be light,' and there was light.
notes: The original Hebrew uses a vav (vocalization) before 'said.' This is a common construction indicating a statement or command. The translation reflects this with 'said,' while maintaining a clear and direct rendering. The 'and' is added for readability, aligning with standard English phrasing.
